subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Descriptive Norms: What Others Do
description: A quick win: understand Descriptive Norms: What Others Do.

hook.text: 'Most guests reuse their towels.' This hotel sign increased towel reuse by 26%. Facts about behavior change behavior.

buildup.text: Descriptive norms tell people what most others do. Humans are social creatures; we follow the herd automatically.

discovery.text: Cialdini's towel study proved that social norms outperform environmental messages.

twist.text: But norms can backfire. Tell heavy energy users they use more than neighbors and they cut back.

climax.text: Pair descriptive norms with an injunctive norm: show what others do plus a smiley face for approval.

punchline.text: Tell people what others do. They'll follow.

quiz.question: What did Cialdini's hotel towel study find?
options: Saying most guests reuse towels increased reuse by 26%

details.summary: Descriptive norms convey information about what most people actually do in a given situation and serve as a powerful nudge by establishing a behavioral standard. Telling people that most of their neighbors conserve energy is more effective than telling them they should conserve.
details.whyItMatters: Descriptive norms are one of the most effective and cost-efficient nudges available. Providing information about typical behavior shifts behavior in contexts from energy conservation to tax compliance to hotel towel reuse without any economic.
takeaways: Telling people what others do is more persuasive than telling them what they should do
Descriptive norm messages reduce energy consumption, increase tax compliance, and improve health behavior
The boomerang effect occurs when high-performers learn the norm is lower than their behavior

faq.question: How does a descriptive norm message differ from a prescriptive one?
faq.answer: A prescriptive message says 'You should conserve energy.' A descriptive norm message says 'Most of your neighbors use 30 percent less energy than you.' The descriptive message is more effective because it provides social proof rather than moralizing.

faq.question: What is the boomerang effect in descriptive norm nudges?
faq.answer: When people who are already doing better than average learn the norm, they sometimes relax their behavior toward the average. Adding an injunctive signal like a smiley face to indicate their behavior is approved prevents this backsliding.
